title: Determining a "Do Not Start" Temperature for a Marathon on the Basis of Adverse Outcomes
population: Race records (starters, finishers, finish-line medical encounters) of several marathons, plotted against start wet bulb globe temperature
findings: A start WBGT above 21 C resulted in a mass-casualty incident or mid-race cancellation in several races.
At the Twin Cities Marathon the rate of 'unsuccessful' starters (medical encounters plus non-finishers) rose rapidly above a start WBGT of 13 C.
The event had an area-wide mass-casualty incident at a start WBGT of 22 C, with an unsuccessful-starter rate of 160 per 1,000 finishers.

The author concludes it seems prudent not to start marathons in unacclimatised northern-latitude fields at a start WBGT above 21 C; the do-not-start WBGT for the Twin Cities Marathon is 20.5 C on this model.
limitations: Outcomes are medical encounters and non-finishes, not finishing time, so the paper does not give a time penalty; northern-latitude events with unacclimatised fields; retrospective race records.
implications: Safety side of road-race heat: unsuccessful starts climbed from a start WBGT of about 13 C and mass-casualty events occurred at 21 to 22 C. Supports a heat warning line at the existing I9 level; not a source of pace penalty.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (MSSE 42:226-232). Abstract read on Europe PMC and PubMed. Crossref lists no correction, erratum or retraction notice (checked 2026-11-16).
